title: Glyoxal-based fixation of Drosophila embryos for immunofluorescence staining and RNA in situ hybridization
protocol: Prepare a scintillation vial for embryo fixation.
Thaw an aliquot of 12% acid-free glyoxal from the -20°C freezer.
Add 3 mL of 0.1M Sodium Phosphate Buffer, pH 7.4 to a glass scintillation vial.
Allow buffer to equilibrate to room temperature (∼22°C).
Add the thawed 1 mL 12% acid-free glyoxal and 4 mL heptane to the scintillation vial.
Swirl the scintillation vial to mix components.
Squirt fresh bleach onto the apple juice plate, completely covering the surface.
Incubate for 30–40 s, swirling occasionally.
Dump the embryos into a stainless steel mesh basket and rinse vigorously with distilled water.
Rinse the apple juice plate with distilled water and dump contents into the basket.
Continue washing the embryos in the basket with a generous amount of water.
Wick away the water by dabbing the basket on a clean paper towel.
Plunge the basket into the heptane/glyoxal mixture in the prepared scintillation vial using tweezers.
Pull out the basket and angle it, shaking carefully so that embryos remain in the vial.
Tightly cap the scintillation vial and secure it on an orbital shaker.
Shake the vial for 1 min at approximately 250 RPMs.
Remove the bottom aqueous phase from the scintillation vial using a glass Pasteur pipet, being careful not to aspirate the embryos.
Add 4 mL of 100% methanol to the embryos and heptane in the scintillation vial.
Tightly cap the vial and touch it briefly to a vortex set at maximum speed for 1 second.
Transfer the popped embryos from the bottom of the vial to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube using a new glass Pasteur pipet.
Avoid transferring any heptane during embryo transfer.
Let the embryos settle by gravity to the bottom of the microcentrifuge tube.
Remove the methanol and discard.
Add 1 mL fresh 100% methanol to wash the embryos.
Let the embryos settle by gravity to the bottom of the tube.
Repeat the methanol wash three times.
Add 1 mL fresh 100% methanol to the embryos.
Incubate overnight (>8 h) at -20°C to complete the fixation.
Transfer glyoxal fixed embryos to a 1.5 mL amber-colored microcentrifuge tube using a glass Pasteur pipet.
Let the embryos settle by gravity to the bottom of the tube.
Remove methanol and discard.
Add 1 ml IF Wash Buffer.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Rinse the embryos one time with IF Wash Buffer as described above.
Wash the embryos four times with IF Wash Buffer as described above.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature (∼22°C).
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Add 1 mL IF Blocking Buffer.
Close the tube and incubate for 1 h with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
In a separate tube, combine appropriate volume of primary antibody with IF Antibody Buffer up to 500 μL.
Add the primary antibody mixture to the blocked embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 4–10 h with gentle nutation at 4°C.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Mix 1 mL IF Wash Buffer and add to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 minutes with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Add 1 μL secondary antibody and combine with IF Antibody Buffer up to 500 μL.
Add the secondary antibody mixture to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 1 hour with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Mix 1 mL IF Wash Buffer and add to the embryos (for two primary antibodies staining).
Close the tube and incubate for 10 minutes with gentle nutation at room temperature (for two primary antibodies staining).
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube (for two primary antibodies staining).
Remove and discard buffer (for two primary antibodies staining).
Add 1 mL IF Wash Buffer for embryo washing.
Close the tube and incubate for 1 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
In a separate tube, combine 1.0 μL 20 mM Hoechst dye with 1.0 mL IF Wash Buffer.
Mix the diluted Hoechst dye mixture thoroughly.
Add 1.0 mL of the diluted Hoechst dye mixture to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 5 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Remove and discard buffer.
Combine 5 μL 5 mg/mL DAPI in 0.5 mL IF Wash Buffer for alternative staining.
Nutate with embryos for 10 min at room temperature.
Add 1 mL IF Wash Buffer for embryo washing.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Repeat washing step four times as described.
Add 200 μL IF Wash Buffer to stained embryos.
Transfer embryos to a slide using a Pasteur pipet.
Wick away excess buffer with the edge of a paper towel.
Add 1 drop of AquaPolymount.
Arrange embryos using a 27G½ needle.
Allow AquaPolymount to harden overnight (>8 h).
Protect stained embryos from light after mounting.
Apply an “X” of AquaPolymount from corner to corner on the coverslip.
Position the coverslip directly over the slide embryo side up.
Gently drop the coverslip straight onto the slide.
Cut a paper towel with dimensions just slightly larger than the slide.
Place the paper towel on the coverslip carefully without moving it.
Lower a 200 G metal analytical weight straight onto the sample.
Let AquaPolymount harden for >1 h to avoid distorting or damaging the embryos.
Clean the coverslip of residual AquaPolymount using a Kimwipe moistened with water before imaging.
Prepare FISH PBS·Triton X-100 buffer just prior to starting the FISH experiment.
Prepare FISH Wash Buffer just prior to starting the FISH experiment.
Prepare FISH SSC·Triton X-100 buffer just prior to starting the FISH experiment.
Confirm an aliquot of FISH Hybridization Buffer is available in the -20°C freezer.
Transfer glyoxal fixed embryos to a 1.5 mL amber-colored microcentrifuge tube using a glass Pasteur pipet.
Let the embryos settle by gravity to the bottom of the tube.
Remove methanol and discard.
Add 1 mL FISH PBS·Triton X-100.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation (or end-over-end rocking) at room temperature (∼22°C).
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Repeat wash step four times.
Add 1 mL FISH PBS·Triton X-100.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation (or end-over-end rocking) at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Rinse the embryos one time with 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer.
Add 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation (or end-over-end rocking) at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Pre-hybridize the embryos two times with 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation (or end-over-end rocking) at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Combine 1 μL 10 μM FISH probes with 49 μL FISH Hybridization Buffer in a separate tube.
Pre-warm the tube containing embryos to room temperature.
Add FISH probe/Hybridization Buffer mixture to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for ∼16 h with gentle nutation at 27°C.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Rinse the embryos one time by adding 1 ml FISH Wash Buffer, allowing them to settle, then removing and discarding buffer.

Wash the embryos two times by adding 1 ml FISH Wash Buffer each time, closing the tube, incubating for 30 min with gentle nutation at 27°C, allowing embryos to settle, and removing and discarding buffer.
Do a serial dilution of Hoechst 33342 dye.
Combine 1 μL of 20 mM Hoechst dye with 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer for a final dilution of 1:1000 Hoechst dye.
Mix the solution thoroughly.
Combine 100 μL of 1:1000 Hoechst dye with 0.9 mL FISH Wash Buffer for a final dilution of 1:10,000 Hoechst dye.
Mix this solution thoroughly.
Add 1 mL of the diluted Hoechst dye mixture to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 30 min with gentle nutation at 27°C.
Allow the embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard the buffer.
Wash the embryos two times as follows: Add 1 mL FISH SSC·Triton X-100 to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow the embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard the buffer after each wash.
Add 200 μL FISH SSC·Triton X-100 to the stained embryos.
Transfer the embryos to a slide using a Pasteur pipet.
Wick away excess buffer with the edge of a paper towel.
Add 1 drop of AquaPolymount and arrange the embryos as desired using a 27G½ needle.
Allow AquaPolymount to harden overnight (>8 h).
Mount the slide embryo side up on a paper towel.
Place an “X” of AquaPolymount from corner to corner of a coverslip of appropriate thickness for the microscope objective that will be used for imaging.
Flip the coverslip over so the AquaPolymount is facing down and position directly over the slide.
Gently drop the coverslip straight onto the slide, making sure it does not slide sideways on the surface of the mounted embryos.
Cut a paper towel with dimensions just slightly larger than the slide.
Place the paper towel on the coverslip carefully to avoid moving it.
Lower a 200 G metal analytical weight straight onto the sample.
Let the AquaPolymount harden for >1 h.
Prepare FISH PBS·Triton X-100, 25 mL.
Prepare FISH-IF Blocking Buffer, 5 mL.
Prepare 1× PBS, 5 mL.
Prepare FISH Wash Buffer, 10 mL.
Transfer fixed embryos to a 1.5 mL amber-colored microcentrifuge tube using a glass Pasteur pipet.
Let the embryos settle by gravity to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard methanol.
Rinse the embryos once with 1 mL FISH PBS·Triton X-100.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Discard buffer after rinsing.
Wash the embryos four times with 1 mL FISH PBS·Triton X-100 each time.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube after each wash.
Discard buffer after each washing step.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature (∼22°C).
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Add 1 mL FISH-IF Blocking Buffer.
Close the tube and incubate for 1 h with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
In a separate tube, combine the appropriate volume of primary antibody and FISH-IF Blocking Buffer up to 500 μL.
Add the primary antibody mixture to the blocked embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 4–10 h with gentle nutation at 4°C.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Wash the embryos four times as follows:
Add 1 mL FISH PBS·Triton X-100.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube. Remove and discard buffer.
Stain the embryos with secondary antibody as follows:
In a separate tube combine 1 μL secondary antibody and FISH-IF Blocking Buffer up to 500 μL.
Add the secondary antibody mixture to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 1 h with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube. Remove and discard buffer.
Wash the embryos four times as follows:
Add 1 mL FISH PBS·Triton X-100.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube. Remove and discard buffer.
Post-fix the embryos as follows:
Add 350 μL of 5 mM BS(PEG)5 in 1× PBS.
Close the tube and incubate for 45 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Add 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Hybridize the embryos with fluorophore labeled FISH probes against your target transcript.
In a separate tube, combine 1 μL 10 μM FISH probes with 49 μL FISH Hybridization Buffer.
Note: If using FISH Hybridization Buffer from the freezer, pre-warm to room temperature.
Add the FISH probe/Hybridization Buffer mixture to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for ∼16 h with gentle nutation at 27°C.
Allow embryos to settle to bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Rinse the embryos one time by adding 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer, allowing embryos to settle and discarding the buffer.
Wash the embryos two times by adding 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer, incubating for 30 minutes with gentle nutation at 27°C, allowing embryos to settle and discarding the buffer.
Do a serial dilution of Hoechst 33342 dye: In a separate tube combine 1 μL 20 mM Hoechst dye with 1 mL FISH Wash Buffer for a final dilution of 1:1000 Hoechst dye, mix.
In another tube combine 100 μL diluted Hoechst dye (1:1000) with 0.9 mL FISH Wash Buffer for a final dilution of 1:10,000 Hoechst dye, mix.
Add 1 mL of the diluted Hoechst dye mixture to the embryos.
Close the tube and incubate for 30 min with gentle nutation at 27°C.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Add 1 mL FISH SSC·Triton X-100.
Close the tube and incubate for 10 min with gentle nutation at room temperature.
Allow embryos to settle to the bottom of the tube.
Remove and discard buffer.
Add 200 μL FISH SSC·Triton X-100 to stained embryos.
Transfer embryos to a slide using a Pasteur pipet.
Wick away excess buffer with the edge of a paper towel.
Add 1 drop of AquaPolymount and arrange embryos as desired using a 27G½ needle.
Allow AquaPolymount to harden overnight (>8 h).
Store stained embryos from light after mounting, but protect them during handling.
Embryos can also be stored overnight at 4°C in FISH SSC·Triton X-100 and mounted on the following day.
Place the slide embryo side up on a paper towel.
Make an “X” of AquaPolymount from corner to corner of a coverslip.
Flip the coverslip over so that the AquaPolymount is facing down and position it directly over the slide.
Gently drop the coverslip straight onto the slide, making sure that it does not slide sideways on the surface of the mounted embryos.
Cut a paper towel with dimensions just slightly larger than the slide.
Place the paper towel on the coverslip, being careful to not move the coverslip.
Lower a 200 G metal analytical weight straight onto the sample.
